Recompute a p-value and/or confidence interval from an already-fitted exact distribution

Source: R/ep-recompute.R
recompute_exact_inference.Rd

Answers a different question about a parameter already fit by ep_multi_shift(), ep_network(), or ep_closed_form(); a different null value beta0, a different significance level alpha, or a different ci_type/direction, directly from that fit's OUTDIST table, without rebuilding the joint distribution. This is possible, and exact (not an approximation), because every algorithm's reference distribution is the same one-dimensional exponential-tilt family, \(\Pr_\beta(T = t) \propto C(t)\, e^{\beta t}\), which sums to one at every value of \(\beta\): re-tilting an already-built C(t) table at a new beta0, or re-deriving a confidence limit at a new alpha, only ever needs that one table, not a new enumeration over the model's stratification and nuisance structure. Building the joint table in the first place is the expensive part of every algorithm in this package; this function is the cheap part, made reusable.

Usage

recompute_exact_inference(
  fit,
  parm,
  beta0 = 0,
  alpha = 0.05,
  ci_type = c("two-sided", "one-sided"),
  direction = c("upper", "lower")
)

Arguments

fit

A fitted object returned by ep_multi_shift(), ep_network(), or ep_closed_form() (any object of class "ep_fit"), i.e. anything with an OUTDIST list and an exactparmest data frame in the format those three functions return.

parm

The name of one parameter already present in fit$OUTDIST/fit$exactparmest$Parameter (e.g. "armvaccinated"); matches the column name exactparmest reports for that term.

beta0

The null value of beta (the log rate ratio) to test against; 0 (the default) reproduces the same null the original fit itself tested. Supply a non-zero value to test a different margin, e.g. log(0.5) for a 50% rate-ratio margin.

alpha

Significance level for the confidence interval; need not match the alpha the original fit used.

ci_type

"two-sided" (default) or "one-sided"; need not match the original fit's own ci_type.

direction

For ci_type = "one-sided": "upper" reports only the upper confidence limit (lower limit fixed at -Inf); "lower" reports only the lower limit (upper limit fixed at Inf). Ignored for ci_type = "two-sided".

Value

A list with:

  • beta0: the null value tested, echoed back.

  • p_lower: the lower tail probability at beta0, \(\Pr_{\beta_0}(T \le t_{obs})\).

  • p_upper: the upper tail probability at beta0, \(\Pr_{\beta_0}(T \ge t_{obs})\).

  • pvalue_two_sided: twice the smaller one-sided tail probability, capped at 1 (the package's two-sided exact p-value convention, matching SAS's PROC GENMOD EXACT statement).

  • pvalue_one_sided: min(p_lower, p_upper).

  • alpha: the significance level used, echoed back.

  • LowerCL, UpperCL: the recomputed confidence limits, on the same scale (beta, the log rate ratio) as fit$exactparmest$Estimate.

See also

ep_multi_shift(), ep_network(), ep_closed_form(), and vignette("Theory-Implementation")'s discussion of reusing an already-built exact distribution.

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  group = c(1L, 1L, 1L, 0L, 0L, 0L),
  age = c(50L, 60L, 70L, 50L, 60L, 70L),
  subjects = c(3492, 2141, 1711, 3525, 2166, 1724),
  cases = c(3, 2, 1, 10, 7, 5),
  futime = c(50, 60, 40, 51, 62, 42)
)
df$lnfutime <- log(df$futime)

fit <- ep_multi_shift(
  formula = cases ~ group,
  data = df,
  offset = "lnfutime",
  offset_log = TRUE,
  strata = "age",
  exact_vars = "group",
  ref_levels = list(group = "0", age = "50"),
  verbose = FALSE
)

# Same question the fit itself already answered (beta0 = 0, alpha = 0.05):
# pvalue_two_sided/LowerCL/UpperCL should match fit$exactparmest exactly.
recompute_exact_inference(fit, "group1")
#> $beta0
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $p_lower
#> [1] 0.002381662
#> 
#> $p_upper
#> [1] 0.9993993
#> 
#> $pvalue_two_sided
#> [1] 0.004763324
#> 
#> $pvalue_one_sided
#> [1] 0.002381662
#> 
#> $alpha
#> [1] 0.05
#> 
#> $LowerCL
#> [1] -2.372642
#> 
#> $UpperCL
#> [1] -0.335739
#> 

# A different confidence level, reusing the same OUTDIST table:
recompute_exact_inference(fit, "group1", alpha = 0.10)
#> $beta0
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $p_lower
#> [1] 0.002381662
#> 
#> $p_upper
#> [1] 0.9993993
#> 
#> $pvalue_two_sided
#> [1] 0.004763324
#> 
#> $pvalue_one_sided
#> [1] 0.002381662
#> 
#> $alpha
#> [1] 0.1
#> 
#> $LowerCL
#> [1] -2.193102
#> 
#> $UpperCL
#> [1] -0.4607849
#>
